THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL COMING ON FOR FURTHER ORDERS, THIS DAY, UMESH M. ADIGA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is directed against the judgment and award passed in M.V.C.No.692/2016 dated 16.10.2018 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Sirsi.
The claimant has field this appeal for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: 2. We refer the parties herein as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. It was the case of the appellant/petitioner that on 11.07.2016 at 9.45 a.m., he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-31-Q-8831 towards Kamaruru Farm, Chandragutti in Soraba Taluk through Banavasi road.
Near Hosakatte of Banavasi, he met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 31-S-7790, which was coming from opposite direction.
Due to the impact, he sustained grievous injuries and while undergoing treatment, his left leg below the knee was amputed.
He had spent more than Rs.5 Lakhs towards treatment and incidental charges.

4. The petitioner has further contended before the Tribunal that he was aged about 60 years at the time of the accident and earning Rs.15,000/- per month by working as Agricultural Farm Supervisor under one Munna Raouf Sab, Banavasi.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident and amputation of left leg, now he is unable to do any work and suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 100%.
With these reasons, he prayed to award compensation of Rs.50 Lakhs.
5. Respondent No.2 had contended before the Tribunal that rider of the offending vehicle had no valid driving license to ride the said vehicle.
The accident had taken place due to negligence of the petitioner.
Liability of Respondent No.2 is restricted to terms and conditions of policy of insurance and holding of valid and effective driving license by rider of the motor cycle.

With these reasons,
prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
7. The petitioner, on his behalf examined PWs-1 to 3 and got marked Exs.P1 to P24.
Respondent No.2 had not lead oral evidence, however, got marked Ex.R1, i.e., policy of insurance.

8. Appreciating the pleadings and evidence, so also hearing the arguments of Advocates for both the parties, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.11,46,837/- under the following heads:

sentences.text: 10. We have heard the arguments of the learned Advocate for the Appellant and Respondent.

Though the matter was posted for hearing on admission of appeal but with the consent of the learned Advocates for both the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.
11.
The learned Advocate for the appellant has contended that the Tribunal has not appreciated the facts properly and awarded meager amount of compensation on all the heads.
The Tribunal has not considered income of the appellant properly.
Therefore, prayed for enhancement of compensation.
12. The leaned Advocate for Respondent No.2 has supported the impugned judgment.

13. The following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether the petitioner/appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?
ii) What order?
14.
The Tribunal has held that accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-31-S-7790 by its rider.
The said fact is not challenged by the respondents.
Therefore, there is no need for re-considering the same.
15. The Tribunal has held that due to injuries sustained in the accident, appellant had sustained injuries and his left leg below the knee was amputated.
This fact is not in dispute.
He had taken treatment as an inpatient for 35 to 40 days and had taken follow up treatment from A.J.Hospital and Research Centre, Mangaluru and other hospitals at Mangaluru.

Looking to the treatment taken as well as amputation of leg,
it appears, petitioner had sustained severe pain and agony.
Therefore the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of "pain and suffering" is on the lower side.
Therefore, Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded under the said head.
16. The claimant/appellant has claimed that he had spent more than Rs.5 lakhs towards medical expenses.
Considering Exs.P6 to P10, the Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.2,26,637/- towards medical expenses.
The learned Advocate for the appellant has contended that the appellant is not highly educated and he is a villager.
He did not maintain all the receipts and in some places, even he did not collect the receipts for purchase of the medicines.
He was admitted as an inpatient and his leg was amputed.
Therefore, he used to send some persons for purchase of the medicines and other articles required for the treatment and they have not collected the receipts.
The said expenses needs to be considered.
The said submissions are sustainable.

Considering the same, Rs.2,50,000/- is Ishwar S/O Venkatramana Naik vs Laxman S/O Keriya Naik on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23687538/
4 awarded towards medical expenses.

sentences.text: 17. The petitioner had taken treatment from different hospitals since he has sustained severe injury to the left leg and later on his leg below knee was amputed; therefore, he might have taken services of Ambulance and taxi to go to one hospital from another for treatment as well as for follow-up treatment.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards conveyance charges, which is on the lower side.
This has to be enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards food and nourishment charges, which is on the lower side.
Considering the treatment taken and his admission in the hospitals as inpatients, Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.

18. The Tribunal, discussing the evidence lead by the petitioner at page No.10 of the impugned judgment, held that the petitioner was not able to prove that he was working as Supervisor in the Farm and earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, on the basis of guess work, the Tribunal has considered the income of the petitioner at Rs.9,000/- per month.
The said finding is tenable.
Merely, petitioner had produced documents and lead evidence of a person said to be a Owner of a Farm land, it cannot be accepted that the said evidence is gospel truth, unless it is corroborated.
There was no corroborative materials to believe the said evidence.
Therefore, the said evidence was rightly rejected by the Tribunal.
That does not call for interference.
Looking to the injuries and treatment taken, he might have lost earning atleast for a period of six months.
The Tribunal has considered for the said purpose as three months, which is erroneous.

Therefore, the - 10 - petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of "loss of income during laid up period"
atleast for a period of six months.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.54,000/- is awarded under the said head.
19. The Tribunal on the basis of the evidence available on record, rightly held that the petitioner has been suffering with permanent disability to an extent of 60%.

On the basis of the said calculation,
the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,83,200/- towards loss of future earning capacity, due to permanent disability.
The said compensation is reasonable.
20. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.1 Lakh towards loss of amenities.
It is to be seen that the petitioner was aged about 60 years at the time of the accident.
He lost his left leg below knee.

Due to the age,
he might be weak.
In addition to that, he lost his one leg below the knee, due to the accident in question.
He has been suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 60% to the whole body as held by the Tribunal.
He has to live with these - 11 - difficulties throughout his life.
He had lost several amenities available to a healthy person.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.1 Lakh was awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of amenities and that is on the lower side.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- is awarded under the said head.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards Attendant Charges.
It is pertinent to note that he was admitted as an inpatient for 35 days in the hospital.
During treatment, his left leg below the knee was amputed.
After discharge from the hospital, he has to depend upon someone to do his day to day work atleast for a period of an year.
Around the clock, someone might be attending him during the said period.
Therefore, amount of Rs.20,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards attendant charges is much on the lower side.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the said head.
